01

“Had We sent down an angel, the matter would have been decided”

An explanation transmitted from Mujāhid ibn Jabr (Q 6:8, 6:9).

262
Explanation from Mujāhid No. 262: 1: 12

Mujāhid ibn Jabr

English
Transmission wording
262: 1:12. Sufyan, from a man, from Mujahid:
"Had We sent down an angel, the matter would have been decided": [that is,] the Hour would have come; "and had We made him an angel, We would have made him a man": they said, "How can an angel be a man?" "and We would have confused them in what they are confusing" (verses 8, 9).
العربية
262: 1: 12 سُفْيَانُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ عَنْ مُجَاهِدٍ وَلَوْ أَنْزَلْنَا مَلَكًا لَقُضِيَ الأَمْرُ لَقَامَتِ السَّاعَةُ وَلَوْ جَعَلْنَاهُ مَلَكًا لجعلناه رجلا فَقَالُوا كَيْفَ يَكُونُ مَلَكٌ رَجُلًا وللبسنا عليهم ما يلبسون (الآية 8، 9) .

03

“and they forbid others from it and keep away from it”

An explanation transmitted from Habib ibn Abi Habib (Q 6:26).

264
Explanation from Habib ibn Abi Habib No. 264: 3: 4

Habib ibn Abi Habib

English
Transmission wording
264: 3:4. Sufyan, from Habib ibn Abi Habib: One who heard Ibn Abbas told me, saying, on the words of God
"and they forbid others from it and keep away from it": He said, it was revealed about Abu ⦗p. 107⦘ Talib, who used to forbid [people] from [harming] the Prophet, peace be upon him, that the Messenger be harmed. He said, "and keep away": he turns away from what he brought. "and they destroy only themselves, though they do not perceive": meaning Abu Talib (verse 26).

04

“You bring these near and keep us away”

An explanation transmitted from Sufyān al-Thawrī (Q 6:52).

265
Explanation from Sufyān No. 265: 4: 5

Sufyān al-Thawrī

English
Transmission wording
265: 4:5. Sufyan, from al-Miqdam ibn Shurayh, from his father, who said:
Sad said, This verse was revealed about six of the Companions of the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, among them Ibn Masud. He said: We used to go early to the Prophet, peace be upon him, and draw near to him. Quraysh said, "You bring these near and keep us away." The Prophet, peace be upon him, was troubled by this, so there was revealed "And do not send away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening," to the end of the verse (verse 52).
العربية
265: 4: 5 سفيان عَنِ الْمِقْدَامِ بْنِ شُرَيْحٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ قَالَ قَالَ سَعْدٌ نَزَلَتْ هَذِهِ الْآيَةُ فِي سِتَّةٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ مِنْهُمُ ابْنُ مَسْعُودٍ قَالَ كُنَّا نَسْبِقُ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ ﷺ وندنو مِنْهُ فَقَالَتْ قُرَيْشٌ تُدْنِي هَؤُلَاءِ وتنحينا ولا فَكَانَ لِلنَّبِيِّ ﷺ هَمٌّ فَنَزَلَتْ وَلا تَطْرُدِ الذين يدعون ربهم بالغدوة والعشي الى آخر الآية (الآية 52) .
Edition record 371346 · p. 107Link to report ↗
05

“We have committed great sins”

An explanation transmitted from Mahan (Q 6:54).

266
Explanation from Mahan No. 266: 5: 9

Mahan

English
Transmission wording
266: 5:9. Sufyan, from Mujammi, from Mahan, who said:
A group came to ⦗p. 108⦘ the Prophet, peace be upon him, and said, "We have committed great sins." The Prophet, peace be upon him, gave them no reply. So there was revealed "And when those who believe in Our verses come to you, say: Peace be upon you. Your Lord has decreed upon Himself mercy." The Messenger of God, peace be upon him, called them and recited it to them (verse 54).

“turn away from them until they enter into another conversation. And…”

An explanation transmitted from Said ibn Jubayr and Abu Malik (Q 6:68).

269
Explanation from Said ibn Jubayr and Abu Malik No. 269: 8: 1

Said ibn Jubayr and Abu Malik

English
Transmission wording
269: 8:1. Abu Hudhayfa related to us; Sufyan related to us, from al-Suddi, from Said ibn Jubayr and Abu Malik:
